## About
Dayton Painter started out as a freelancer doing Volkswagen engine work, like lifter repair and cylinder head reconditioning, out of a small shop behind his friend's shop. He later moved to a larger shop on Custer Street, and the business grew from there. Dayton passed away, and members of his family now run the business.
The shop has expanded to offer a full range of services for air-cooled Volkswagen engines: repair, engine rebuilding and machine work. We work on water-cooled VWs too.
Ross Maitland is a mechanic and machinist who grew up around his dad's Beetle and Westfalia campers, and he owns a restored ragtop Beetle. Eddie Radillo is our transmission builder and a lifelong drag racing enthusiast. Keith Gosselin, engine builder and mechanic, got his start working on a Baja Bug and is into off-road racing.
We're rated 4.8 from 168 Google reviews. One customer picked up his bug after a new clutch and muffler and said it rides and sounds sweet.

## Services
- Machine Shop Services: A full range of precision machine work on cases, flywheels, cranks, rods, lifters and cylinder heads for various VW engine types, including waterboxer.
- Engine & Transmission Rebuilding: Engine and transmission rebuilds for air-cooled VWs, with rebuilt transaxles kept in stock for exchange.
- General Repair & Services: Brakes, oil changes, engine and transmission removal and replacement, and a variety of other mechanical repairs.
- Air-cooled vs. Water-cooled: We work on both air-cooled and water-cooled VWs.
- VW parts: One reviewer calls us a good place to buy parts, and we handle parts orders by email.

## FAQ
Q: What is the difference between air-cooled and water-cooled?
A: Air cooling directs airflow at fins on the cylinders and heads, so heat goes straight into the air. Water-cooled engines circulate coolant around the heads and cylinders through a water jacket and use a separate radiator for the final heat exchange to the air.

Q: Do you work on water-cooled VWs?
A: Yes. Our focus is air-cooled engines, but we work on both air-cooled and water-cooled VWs.

Q: Do you have rebuilt transaxles available?
A: We keep rebuilt transaxles in stock for exchange. Call the shop to talk through what you need.

Q: Are you open on Saturdays?
A: Saturday hours are seasonal. Starting November 7 we close on Saturdays for the winter, and regular Saturday hours resume in April. If you need help outside our schedule, give us a call.

Q: What should I include when emailing about a parts order?
A: Include your name, phone number, order number and the date you purchased your parts, and a customer service representative will contact you.
